(p-627) Surah "al-Tariq"

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿By the sky and the Tariq!﴾ ﴿And what will make you know what the Tariq is?﴾ ﴿It is the piercing star.﴾ He magnified the station of the sky in the eyes of creatures, because it is the source (ma'din) of their provision, the dwelling of His angels, and in it is the creation of Paradise. So He swore by it, and by the Tariq. What is meant is the category of stars, or the category of meteors (shuhub) with which devils are pelted, because of the greatness of their benefit. Then He explained it as "the piercing star," i.e., the bright one, as if it pierces the darkness with its light and penetrates into it. It is described as "Tariq" because it appears at night, just as the one who comes at night is called "tariq," or because it strikes the jinn, i.e., it hits them. The answer to the oath is:

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 86, verse 4:

﴿Indeed, every soul has over it a guardian.﴾ Because "lammā" (لَمّا), if it is read with a shadda (emphatic doubling) in the sense of "illā" (إلّا, "except"), as in the reading of ʿĀṣim, Ḥamza and Ibn ʿĀmir, then "in" (إنْ) is a negation, meaning: "Not every soul except that over it is a guardian." If it is read without the shadda, as in the reading of the others, then "in" is the light form of the heavy "inna" (إنَّ), meaning: indeed every soul, surely over it is a guardian who protects it from calamities, or who protects its deeds, its provision and its term of life; when it completes that, it dies. It has also been said that he is the recorder of deeds. Then "mā" (ما) is superfluous (zāʾida), the lām is the distinguishing particle (lām al-fāriqa) between the heavy and the light, "ḥāfiẓun" (حافِظٌ) is the subject (mubtadaʾ), "ʿalayhā" (عَلَيْها) is the predicate (khabar), and the whole clause is the predicate of "kull" (كُلُّ). Whichever of the two readings is adopted, it is among those things that are preceded by the oath (yutalaqqā bihi al-qasam).

(p-628) ﴿So let man consider from what he was created.﴾ When He mentioned that over every soul there is a guardian, He commanded him to reflect upon the beginning of his affair, so that he would know that the One who originated him is able to restore him and to requite him, and so that he would act for the Day of Recompense, and would not dictate to his guardian anything except what would please him in his final outcome. "Mimma khuliqa" (from what was he created) is an interrogative: that is, "From what thing was he created?!" Its answer is:

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 86, verse 6:

﴿He was created from a gushing fluid﴾. Al-dafq (the act of pouring forth) means pouring out with propulsion. Strictly speaking, al-dafq belongs to its possessor (the one who emits it), and attributing it to the water is a metaphor (majaz). It is related from some of the people of lexicography: "dafaqtu al-ma'a dafqan," meaning "I poured the water," and "dafaqa al-ma'u bi-nafsihi," meaning "the water gushed out by itself," i.e., it flowed forth. He did not say "from two waters" (min ma'ayn), because the two fluids mix together in the womb and unite at the time when his creation begins.

"It comes out from between the backbone and the ribs." From between the backbone of the man and the ribs of the woman. The ribs (tara'ib) are the bones of the chest, where the necklace rests. It has been said: the bone and the sinew come from the man, and the flesh and the blood come from the woman.

**﴿Indeed He﴾**: indeed the Creator, because of the indication of "created" (*khuliqa*) [in the preceding verse], is referring to Him. Its meaning: indeed He who created man at first from a drop (*nutfah*),

**﴿is able to return him﴾**: is able to bring him back (*i'adah*) in particular,

**﴿certainly﴾**: clearly possessing power, not incapable of it, like the saying (of the Qur'an) "Indeed I am certainly in need" (*la-faqir*).

"And ﴿the Day when secrets are tested﴾ is in the accusative (nusiba), i.e., it is uncovered (tukshafu), governed by "rij'ihi" (His returning), or by an implied verb indicated by His saying "rij'ihi," i.e., His resurrection (mab'athuhu).

﴿The secrets﴾: what is concealed in the hearts of creeds and intentions, and what is hidden of deeds."

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 86, verse 10:

﴿So what for him﴾: what for the human being,

﴿of power﴾: in himself, to repel what has befallen him,

﴿nor any helper﴾: who would aid him and ward off (the harm) from him.

By the sky which returns (with rain),

Al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) comments: "Ar-raj' (the returning) is the rain, and it is so called because it returns again and again at every time."
ﷻ"By the earth, which splits open": that is, what the earth splits open to bring forth of plants.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 86, verse 13:

﴿Indeed it﴾: that is, the Qur'an,

﴿is a decisive word﴾: one that separates truth from falsehood, just as it is called "al-Furqan" (the Criterion).

"And it is not a jest," that is, not play or falsehood. It means that it is entirely serious. It is part of its due, and God has described it so, that it should be awe-inspiring in hearts and held in esteem in souls, such that its reciter and listener are elevated by it, and that they should not indulge in jesting or amuse themselves with levity.

(p-629) ﴿Indeed they﴾, meaning the polytheists of Makkah,

﴿are plotting a plot﴾, they devise schemes to nullify the command of Allah and to extinguish the light of the Truth.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 86, verse 16:

﴿And I plot a plot.﴾ I will requite them for their plotting by drawing them on gradually (istidraj) from where they do not know. So the requital of the plot is called "a plot," just as the requital of transgression and of an evil deed is called "transgression" and "an evil deed," even though it is not really transgression and evil deed. This description may not be applied to God (Exalted is He) except in the sense of requital, as in His saying: ﴿They forgot God, so He forgot them﴾ [al-Tawbah: 67]; ﴿They seek to deceive God, but He is the One who deceives them﴾ [al-Nisa': 142]; ﴿God mocks them﴾ [al-Baqarah: 15].

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 86, verse 17:

﴿So give respite to the disbelievers﴾, that is: do not call down their destruction, and do not seek to hasten it.

﴿Give them respite﴾: allow them time. He repeated it, but varied the wording between the two expressions, for the sake of added calming and consolation.

﴿Gently﴾: a brief respite. It is never spoken except in the diminutive form (رويدا, ruwayda), and it derives from "رادت الريح، ترود، رودا" (the wind moved gently), meaning it moved with a weak motion.
